question: A developer uses Claude to generate a database migration script intended for a production system with live customer data. What is the appropriate next step before running the script?
options: A) Ask Claude to shorten the script so it executes faster during the production maintenance window
B) Run the script directly in production because Claude generated syntactically valid SQL for the target database
C) Have an engineer review and test the script against a staging environment before running it in production
D) Paste the script into a chat message so the team can read it before the deployment window closes
correct_answers: C) Have an engineer review and test the script against a staging environment before running it in production
explanations: Incorrect. Optimizing for execution speed does not address whether the migration logic is correct or safe to run against live data.
Incorrect. Valid syntax only confirms the script will run, not that its logic is correct or safe for the specific production schema and data.
Correct. A migration against live production data is an irreversible, high-impact action, so an engineer should review the logic and test it in staging before it ever touches production.
Incorrect. Simply pasting the script for others to glance at is not equivalent to a structured review and staging test before a production change.
